name: Team Fuel Fundraiser
oneLiner: A fundraising storefront where hockey teams, schools, soccer clubs, cadets and community groups each get their own J&W page, share link and live progress bar, and families buy freezer packs and Meal Butler meals with the group's share shown under every price.
headline: It turns the families around a team or school into J&W customers for about $33 each, paid to the group instead of to Meta, and every order is pre-sold and delivered in one drop on a route J&W already drives.
focus: Community fundraising that brings new households to J&W
mechanism: Each school, team, club or community group gets its own J&W team page with a share link, per-player links and a live progress bar. Families buy a short menu at regular store prices: a Team Freezer Pack ($167.50: Premium Chicken Burgers 25-pack $35.50 + 4 kg portioned chicken breast case $92 + Ground Beef Bulk Mix 5 lb $40), a Meal Butler Game-Week Meal Pack ($122.40: 10 cooked 4 oz pre-set meals + 2 Egg White Bites), the Kids Favourite Combo ($95) and the Long Weekend Box ($199). J&W pays the group 20% on Meal Butler and 12% on butcher items from its own margin, shown under every price ($20.10 on the Freezer Pack, $24.48 on the Game-Week Pack), plus 5% on team-link orders for six months after the drop. Orders close on a Sunday and arrive in one labelled drop at the arena or hall on J&W's existing route day (free, no minimum), or families pick up free at 2201 Brimley Rd or take home delivery at the usual fee. Every buyer is asked for CASL consent and offered $10 off a first regular order, and groups get a free 'Fuel for Game Day' talk at $1,500 in sales and a raffle box at $3,000.

modelledOn.name: Halenda's Fundraising
modelledOn.short: Durham family butcher's meat-stick fundraiser for schools and teams
modelledOn.what: Halenda's Meats (family-owned since 1979; five Durham stores plus St Jacobs Market; plants in Oshawa and Etobicoke) runs a school and team fundraising program on one product, Pepperoni Stix. Groups buy a case of 240 sticks (24 bags of 10) for $261-$300 and sell each bag at $25, keeping 50-56%. Shipping is $18 a case anywhere in Ontario, pick-up is free. Two modes: 'order the sticks, then sell' (about 95% of groups) and 'collect orders, then buy' with a personalised flyer and order form (about 5%). The site has a two-way profit calculator, a tier table, a sales-rep field on the order form, a school-compliance FAQ and segment success stories.
modelledOn.proof: First case shipped June 27, 2013; 6 million+ meat sticks sold and 'more than six million dollars' raised for groups (post of Nov 6, 2025). Implied about 450K sticks, 1,880 cases and $0.5M of wholesale revenue a year (ESTIMATE, competitor-07.md). Recent stories: a Newcastle dance studio raised $10,300 (Sept 2026); a 12-year-old BJJ athlete sold 8 cases in a month and raised $1,536 (Aug 2026). Fundraising pages updated Sept 23, 2026. Group count and company revenue not found.
modelledOn.jwEdge: Halenda's sells cases to the group, which resells bags for cash, so supporters never become Halenda's customers. J&W sells to each family directly on a team page, with consent, so every buyer becomes a J&W customer. Baskets are bigger and are food families already buy: a typical $135 J&W order sends about $21 to the group against $12.50-$14.13 per $25 bag, with no upfront case purchase. J&W adds pork-free packs (the Halenda's stick is pork), cooked Meal Butler meals for sports weeks, its own weekly routes including the Tuesday Durham route past every Halenda's store, and one storefront with current prices instead of three domains with conflicting price tables. Halenda's stays ahead on track record, field reps, awards and a shelf-stable hand-sell product, and groups keep 50-56% there versus 12-20% at J&W.

mathYear1: Campaigns ramp 0 -> 42 by drop month (Nov 0, Dec 4, Jan 3, Feb 4, Mar 5, Apr 6, May 6, Jun 3, Jul 1, Aug 1, Sep 4, Oct 5). Fundraiser sales: 42 campaigns x 25 orders x $135 = $141,750 x 0.80 incremental = $113,400. Follow-on: 1,050 orders x 0.9 unique = 945 households x 70% new = 662 x 12% become repeat = 79 x 4 orders/yr x $130 x 5.26 avg months left / 12 = $18,100 x 0.85 = $15,385. Year 1 = $113,400 + $15,385 = $128,785 (about $129K). Low: 25 x 18 x $125 x 0.75 = $42,188 + follow-on $3,803 = $46K. High: 60 x 32 x $140 x 0.85 = $228,480 + follow-on $42,638 = $271K.
mathRunRate: Year 2: 85 campaigns (about 27 returning groups x 1.5 campaigns + 45 new) x 27 orders x $138 = $316,710 x 0.80 = $253,368. Follow-on: year-1 repeaters 79 x 60% still active x 4 x $130 = $24,767, plus year-2 new households 85 x 27 x 0.9 x 65% = 1,343 x 12% = 161 x 4 x $130 x 5.67/12 = $39,589; ($24,767 + $39,589) x 0.85 = $54,702. Run-rate = $253,368 + $54,702 = $308,070 (about $308K).
mathNotes: Revenue is counted at full store price. The group share is a cost inside the margin, not a discount: 55% raw at 30% margin + 45% Meal Butler at 45% = 36.75% blended; average group share 55% x 12% + 45% x 20% = 15.6% (about $21 on a $135 order); margin after the share 21.15%. Follow-on orders earn 36.75% less 5% on the ~60% placed through the team link = 33.75%.

Displacement is charged too: the 20% of fundraiser sales existing customers would have placed anyway now carries the group share ($28,350 x 15.6% = $4,423 in year 1; $9,881 in year 2). Gross profit after share and displacement: year 1 $24,754 (19% of counted revenue), year 2 $62,168 (20%), hence marginPct 20.

Contribution after J&W's running costs: year 1 $24,754 - $22,066 running - $3,200 setup = about -$0.5K (break-even); year 2 $62,168 - $40,000 = about +$22K. The real return is about 2,000 new households in two years (662 + 1,343).
Group share per new household: $22,113 / 662 = about $33 in year 1 and $37 in year 2, against $60-120 paid-ads CAC (model-assumptions.md).

Monthly shape, year 1 gross booked: Nov $0, Dec $13.5K, Jan $10.5K, Feb $14.1K, Mar $17.8K, Apr $21.6K, May $22.1K, Jun $12.4K, Jul $5.9K, Aug $6.0K, Sep $16.2K, Oct $19.9K = $159.9K gross, $128.8K after incrementality.

Sanity: year 1 is about 5% of J&W's ~$2.5M mid-case revenue, run-rate about 12%. Halenda's implied ~1,880 cases a year at an assumed 6 cases per group is roughly 300 campaigns a year (group count not found); J&W's 85 in year 2 is about 28% of that, across a wider route area. The GTHL alone has 493 teams.
Trimmed from the selection's year-2 idea (100 groups x $4,000 plus a $0.16-0.31M DTC tail), as competitor-07.md advised: only two buyer cohorts exist by year 2, so the follow-on tail is about $55K.

Not counted: Team Fuel Jerky (in development), and any later Butcher Club (Play 3), Goal Plan (Play 1), AI Coach (Play 6), gifting (Play 5), At Work (Play 4) or wholesale (Play 2) revenue from fundraiser buyers or clubs. Follow-on here is one-time regular orders only; the 0.85 factor partly covers overlap.

assumptions: Lean storefront live by Mon Nov 23, 2026 (Shopify team pages, an attribution app, a share ledger); 4 pilot groups recruited from J&W's own customers who coach, teach or sit on parent councils.
42 campaigns in year 1 and 85 in year 2; 70% of groups return and run about 1.5 campaigns a year.
25 orders per campaign at $135 in year 1; 27 at $138 in year 2.
Product mix 55% raw (30% margin) and 45% Meal Butler (45% margin), per model-assumptions.md; average group share 15.6%.
Group share rates (Concept): 20% Meal Butler cooked, 12% butcher boxes and cases, 5% on team-link orders for 6 months after the drop.
0.9 unique households per order; 70% new to J&W in year 1, 65% in year 2.
12% of new households become repeat customers ordering 4 times a year at $130; 60% of year-1 repeaters still active in year 2.
Incrementality 0.80 on fundraiser sales (about 30% of buyers are existing customers shifting some orders) and 0.85 on follow-on.
60% of follow-on orders use the team link; 25% of new households redeem the $10 welcome offer.
About 60% of campaigns pass $1,500 in sales (free talk) and 45% pass $3,000 (raffle box, about $139 at cost).
Team drops only on GTA routes 1-4, minimum 12 orders; long-route areas use home delivery or a group drop for 40+ orders.
J&W confirms the $35.50 price and margin of the 25-pack chicken burgers and fixes the 5 lb vs 10 lb ground beef listing before launch.
risks: Group share (12-20%) is far below Halenda's 50-56%: lead with dollars per order (about $21 vs $12.50-$14.13 per bag), fewer sales per family, no upfront cash and food families already buy; if pilots stall, raise the Meal Butler rate to 25% (J&W still keeps about 20%).
Thin margin (about 21% after the share): keep the menu short, drops on existing route days, a 12-order minimum for a team drop, and track contribution per campaign.

Product data: the 25-pack chicken burgers at $35.50 (about $3.79/lb) may sit below the 30% margin model; the ground beef listing says 5 lb in the title and 10 lb in the description with a 'GROUNDPORK' photo; J&W's 'salt and sugar free' line conflicts with some ingredient lists (Beef Chili lists brown sugar and salt). Fix before launch and make no blanket salt or sugar claims on fundraiser pages.

Schools: board fundraising rules and Ontario's school food and beverage policy (PPM 150) may apply to food sold through a school; send a one-page school pack and default schools to Brimley pickup or home delivery until the board approves a school drop.
Cold chain at drops: coolers, a J&W staffer on site for the whole window, uncollected orders back to Brimley the same day and held 3 days.
Children's privacy: first name, last initial and jersey number only, families can hide their name, unlisted non-indexed pages, organizers never see buyers' contact details.
CASL: J&W messages only buyers with express consent; organizers send campaign messages to their own contacts; drop-day texts are transactional.
Allergens and dietary needs: answers only from approved per-product data or a person; the Long Weekend Box includes sausages and ribs; no halal or kosher labels.
Tax and accounting: the group payment is a marketing cost, not a charitable gift, and buyers get no tax receipts; J&W's accountant confirms recording and any HST question.
December overlap with corporate gifting (Play 5): cap the pilot at 4 groups with Tuesday and Wednesday drops.
Owner-led brand risk: schools and faith groups will look J&W up; show the 4.8 star Google rating (611 reviews) and keep the coordinator as the program's face.
Team Fuel Jerky needs a tested recipe, shelf-life work and approval under the provincial licence; treat it as a 2027 project and do not count it.
who: Fundraising coordinator (Tasia or Lucas, as J&W decides): about 3 h/week in the December pilot, 5 h/week on average in year 1, 8 h/week in year 2, approving team pages and agent drafts, calling organizers, booking talks and running drops. Driver: about 1.5 h per drop on the existing route day (42 drops in year 1, 85 in year 2). Packer: about 2 minutes per order for named bags plus 30 minutes per drop. Butcher or Lucas: 1.5 h per 'Fuel for Game Day' talk, about 2 a month. Owner (Bill or Steve): about 15 minutes a week approving payouts over $500 and new school partners. Minastech builds the storefront and the agents.

costs.note: Setup about $3,200: pack photos and team-kit design $800; insulated totes, name labels, stickers and 4 drop coolers $900; pilot tasting trays and printed school pack $500; Shopify setup 20 h x $25 = $500; label printer $300; first flyers $200. Year 1 running about $22.1K ($1,840/month average): coordinator 5 h/wk x 48 x $25 = $6,000; 42 drops x $67 van and packer time = $2,814; named bags and labels 1,050 orders x $2.33 = $2,447; 25 coach talks x $70 = $1,750; 19 raffle boxes x $139 at cost = $2,641; Meta ads $200 x 11 = $2,200; flyers 42 x $40 = $1,680; software (attribution app, payout fees, Claude API) $80 x 11 = $880; welcome offers 662 x 25% x $10 = $1,654. Year 2 running about $40K. The group share itself (about $22.1K in year 1, $49.4K in year 2) and the 5% team-link share sit inside the margin, not in this list. Excludes Minastech's fee.

prototype.concept: A fundraising front door J&W does not have today. Organizers see what their group earns, work out a goal in two taps, and get a team page that an AI agent drafts in seconds. Parents and supporters use a real-feeling team page for the fictional Scarborough Snowhawks U11 AA: a scoreboard progress bar, the group's share under every price, a player picker, and checkout on J&W's real routes with a free team drop. The JW team view shows the December 2026 pilot: live campaigns, agent drafts to approve, the drop sheet, production and route impact, payouts, and the new customers the program brings in.
prototype.wow: On the Snowhawks team page a parent picks 'Maya R. #14' and taps Add on the Team Freezer Pack. The sticky bar shows '$20.10 to the Snowhawks' and a striped pending segment appears on top of the $456.12 already raised. After the demo checkout the segment fills in, the total counts up to $476.22, orders tick from 22 to 23, Maya's shout-out goes from 3 to 4 orders, and a thank-you card says exactly what this order sent to the team.

design.inspiredBy: Halenda's Fundraising (halendasfundraising.com): white utility bar with an outlined CTA pill, full-bleed photo hero with a dark overlay and centred white headline, short coloured rules under centred section titles, a light-blue two-way profit calculator card, a plain tier table, a numbered order block, an objection-handling FAQ and segment stories, with Raleway headings and Playfair serif accents. J&W's version adds what Halenda's lacks: per-team pages with a scoreboard progress bar, the share under every price (Rowe Farms idea), per-player links, one storefront with current prices, and rink and pitch line drawings in place of team photos. No Halenda's text, logos or photos.

design.layout: Mobile-first single column, 16px gutters, max width 1120px. Fonts: https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?family=Big+Shoulders+Display:wght@700;800&family=Instrument+Serif:ital@0;1&family=Inter:wght@400;500;600;700&display=swap (Big Shoulders Display uppercase for headings and scoreboard numerals, Instrument Serif italic for one accent line per section, Inter body with tabular numbers in money). White utility bar under the concept bar: J&W logo ../assets/img/jw-logo.jpg (36px) + 'TEAM FUEL' wordmark and an outlined ember pill 'Start a fundraiser'. Centred section titles with a 40px ember rule. Hero: full-bleed chicken-burger photo under a rink-night gradient, centred headline; the 'at a glance' card overlaps the hero bottom on mobile and sits right of the headline on desktop. Team page: rink-night scoreboard band (crest circle with initials, big numerals, 14px progress bar with gold goal tick, sky rink-line SVG behind), pack cards 1 column on mobile, 2 on tablet, 4 on desktop; add-ons in a horizontal snap rail with the next card peeking. Sticky bottom bar on mobile while the team page is in view (items, total, share, 'Review order'), 52px, above the framework dock. Tables become stacked cards under 640px. Tap targets 44px. No horizontal scroll at 375px.
design.tone: Warm, local and practical, written for volunteer parents who are short on time. Short sentences, Canadian spelling, plain numbers, no hype, no pile-up of exclamation marks. A family butcher talking to a hockey parent at the rink.

sections.name: S9 Questions organizers ask
sections.purpose: Objection handling before a principal or club board says yes
sections.content: id 'faq', accordion. 'Do we have to pre-buy anything?' 'No. Families pay J&W online when they order. You never hold cash or product.' / 'When do we get paid?' 'Within 10 business days of your drop, by e-transfer or cheque, with a statement of every order.' / 'Is this a donation? Do buyers get tax receipts?' 'No. Your group's share is a fundraising payment from J&W, not a charitable donation, so we don't issue tax receipts.' / 'Can you deliver to our school?' 'School boards have their own fundraising and food rules. We send your principal a one-page school pack. Until your board says yes to a school drop, families can pick up free at Brimley Rd or choose home delivery.' / 'What if a family misses the drop?' 'We take their order back to Brimley Rd frozen and hold it 3 days for free pickup (Mon–Fri 9–6, Sat 10–4).' / 'Allergies, pork and halal?' 'Every pack comes with an ingredient and allergen sheet before your campaign starts, and our coordinator confirms anything specific. The Freezer Pack, Game-Week Pack and Kids Combo list no pork. The Long Weekend Box includes sausages and ribs. We don't label packs halal or kosher.' / 'Can relatives outside Ontario help?' 'Yes, if the food stays here. We deliver only in Ontario because our plant is provincially inspected. A grandparent in BC can buy a pack for a team family to pick up at the drop.' / 'How long should a campaign run?' 'Two weeks works well: open on a Monday, close on a Sunday, drop the next week on our route day.' / 'Where do you do team drops?' 'On our weekly routes: Tuesday in Durham (Pickering to Port Perry), Wednesday in Toronto, Scarborough, North York, Etobicoke and Mississauga, Thursday from Oakville to Hamilton, Friday in York and Peel. Farther away, families choose home delivery on our long routes.'

chat.name: Team Fuel Desk
chat.greeting: Hi, I'm the Team Fuel Desk. I can work out how many orders your group needs, explain how drops and payouts work, or answer a parent's question. Is your group a team, a school or a club?
suggestions: How much does our group earn?
How many orders for a $1,000 goal?
Can you deliver to our arena?

rules.reply: We don't answer allergy questions from memory. Every pack comes with an ingredient and allergen sheet before your campaign starts, and our coordinator will confirm anything specific at (416) 298-1350. On pork: the Team Freezer Pack, Game-Week Meal Pack and Kids Favourite Combo list no pork. The Long Weekend Box includes sausages and ribs. We don't label our packs halal or kosher.

Your group's share is a fundraising payment from J&W to your group, not a charitable donation, so buyers don't get tax receipts. Your group gets a statement of every order, and the money arrives by e-transfer or cheque within 10 business days of the drop.

We can only deliver in Ontario, because our meat plant is provincially inspected. Relatives outside Ontario can still help: they buy a pack for a team family, and it's picked up at the drop here. The food never leaves the province.

School boards have their own fundraising and food rules, so we send your principal a one-page school pack with the product list and allergen sheets. Until your board says yes to a school drop, families can pick up free at 2201 Brimley Rd or choose home delivery on their route day.

We bring every order, bagged and labelled by name, to one spot on our route day for your area: Tuesday in Durham, Wednesday in Toronto, Scarborough and Mississauga, Thursday from Oakville to Hamilton, Friday in York and Peel. A J&W staffer stays for a 60-minute pickup window. Team drops have no fee and no $100 minimum. If a family misses it, we hold their order frozen at Brimley Rd for 3 days.

At about $21 for your group on a typical $135 order, a $1,000 goal is about 48 orders. For 16 families that's 3 each: your own freezer fill plus two supporters. Try the goal calculator on this page with your own numbers. These are estimates, not a promise.

Nothing up front. Families pay J&W online when they order, so you never collect cash or store product. After the drop we send your group a statement of every order and pay your share by e-transfer or cheque within 10 business days.

Three extras. At $1,500 in sales, a J&W butcher brings a free 30-minute 'Fuel for Game Day' talk and a tasting tray to a practice (general food tips, not medical advice). At $3,000, we add a Long Weekend Box ($199) for your raffle. And for six months after your drop, orders through your team link still send 5% to your group.

We're working on a J&W-made jerky that players could sell by hand, but it isn't for sale yet. It needs a tested recipe, shelf-life testing and approval under our provincial licence. Leave your email in the 'Coming next' card and we'll tell you when it's ready.

Your group earns 20% on Meal Butler cooked packs and 12% on butcher boxes, freezer packs and cases, shown under every price. That's about $21 on a typical $135 order. Families pay our regular store prices; the share comes from our side. For six months after your drop, orders through your team link still send 5%.
